1.1.text:
Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tual City.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and Regional House of Representatives according to the principle of autonomy and Co-Administration Task with the principle of the broadest possible autonomy within the system and principle of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Mayor is the Mayor of Tual.
5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Implementation is all actions carried out by government and non-government institutions which include prevention, protection and recovery for victims of violence against women and children.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, and not yet married including a child still in the womb.
8. Woman is every person who is physically born as a woman.
9. Victim is a woman and or child who experiences suffering and or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Prevention is all efforts carried out by government and non-government institutions aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children.
11. Child protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Women protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Suffering is any act that results in or can result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.
14. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting or causing death.
15. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling helpless, and or severe psychological suffering to women and or children.
16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
17. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim, when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
18. Companion is a person or institution that has the ability to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, legal services and advocacy for strengthening victim recovery.
19. Women and child protection institution is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (Including Medicolegal), psycho-social and legal services.
20. Safe house is temporary housing used to provide protection to women and children victims in accordance with the standard operating procedures or abbreviated as SOP that are determined.
21. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or other community organizations.
22. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, hospital-based, community health centers, P2TP2A, Safe Houses, Child Social Protection Houses (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection Houses (RPTC), Women's Social Protection Houses (RPSW).
23. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence in a comprehensive and quality manner.

Article 14

(1) Forms of protection for women and children victims of violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), psychological protection, repatriation and social reintegration.

(2) Forms of medical protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1). Consist of treatment and recovery of physical wounds aimed at recovering the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(3) Forms of legal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.

(5) Forms of psychological protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of assistance in the framework of recovery of traumatic conditions of victims including the provision of Safe Houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.

(6) Forms of Repatriation protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

(7) Forms of Social Reintegration protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to reunite women and children victims of violence with family, substitute family.

Article 2

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is aimed at providing prevention, protection and services to women and children from acts of violence.

Article 13

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for residents of Tual City both in Tual City and outside Tual City.

Article 9

(1) In the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which includes prevention and mitigation activities, an Integrated Service Center (PPT) shall be established.

(2) The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements of the Regional Government and elements from related institutions outside the Regional Government.

(3) Further provisions regarding the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be further regulated by Mayor Regulation.

(4) The PPT as referred to in Paragraph (1), in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence may coordinate with institutions and or organizations in Tual City.

(5) In the Implementation of Protection for women and children victims of violence, it may be established at the sub-district, urban village and village levels.

Article 10

(1) In addition to establishing the PPT as referred to in Article 9, to support the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, the regional government may establish P2TP2A.

(2) The P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements of the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Health Service, Social Service, Ministry of Religious Affairs, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Service, NGOs, Child Observers.

(3) The P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), is a functional work unit having the task of implementing integrated services for women and children victims of violence.

(4) In carrying out the main tasks and functions as referred to in paragraph (3), the P2TP2A may coordinate and become a working partner of the PPT. (5) Further provisions regarding the P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4), shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 16

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in article 15 paragraph (2), shall be provided guidance by the regional government through regional apparatus organizations related to the tasks of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) Organizational guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may consist of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

(1) The regional government is obligated to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence. (2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of:

Article 15

(1) The Government in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence. May involve community participation. (2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1), may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

c. fast, safe and empathetic;
d. existence of confidentiality guarantee;

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

(1) The funding source for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence conducted by the regional apparatus of Tual City is from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Tual City.

(2) The funding source as referred to in paragraph (1), may also come from other legitimate and non-binding sources.

(3) The funding source for implementation from other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be supervised in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) PPT is required to report the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence periodically to the Mayor of Tual in accordance with applicable regulations.

1.3.text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tual City.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and Regional House of Representatives according to the principle of autonomy and Co-Administration Task with the principle of the broadest possible autonomy within the system and principle of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Mayor is the Mayor of Tual.
5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Implementation is all actions carried out by government and non-government institutions which include prevention, protection and recovery for victims of violence against women and children.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, and not yet married including a child still in the womb.
8. Woman is every person who is physically born as a woman.
9. Victim is a woman and or child who experiences suffering and or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Prevention is all efforts carried out by government and non-government institutions aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children.
11. Child protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Women protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Suffering is any act that results in or can result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.
14. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting or causing death.
15. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling helpless, and or severe psychological suffering to women and or children.
16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
17. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim, when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
18. Companion is a person or institution that has the ability to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, legal services and advocacy for strengthening victim recovery.
19. Women and child protection institution is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (Including Medicolegal), psycho-social and legal services.
20. Safe house is temporary housing used to provide protection to women and children victims in accordance with the standard operating procedures or abbreviated as SOP that are determined.
21. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or other community organizations.
22. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, hospital-based, community health centers, P2TP2A, Safe Houses, Child Social Protection Houses (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection Houses (RPTC), Women's Social Protection Houses (RPSW).
23. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence in a comprehensive and quality manner.

Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.

Article 14

(1) Forms of protection for women and children victims of violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), psychological protection, repatriation and social reintegration.

(2) Forms of medical protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1). Consist of treatment and recovery of physical wounds aimed at recovering the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(3) Forms of legal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.

(5) Forms of psychological protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of assistance in the framework of recovery of traumatic conditions of victims including the provision of Safe Houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.

(6) Forms of Repatriation protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

(7) Forms of Social Reintegration protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to reunite women and children victims of violence with family, substitute family.

Article 2

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is aimed at providing prevention, protection and services to women and children from acts of violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 9

(1) In the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which includes prevention and mitigation activities, an Integrated Service Center (PPT) shall be established.

(2) The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements of the Regional Government and elements from related institutions outside the Regional Government.

(3) Further provisions regarding the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be further regulated by Mayor Regulation.

(4) The PPT as referred to in Paragraph (1), in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence may coordinate with institutions and or organizations in Tual City.

(5) In the Implementation of Protection for women and children victims of violence, it may be established at the sub-district, urban village and village levels.

Article 13

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for residents of Tual City both in Tual City and outside Tual City.

Article 15

(1) The Government in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence. May involve community participation. (2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1), may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

Article 18

(1) The regional government is obligated to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence. (2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of:

a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 11

(1) The Implementation of Protection for victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner in medical handling, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which may be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.

(2) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(3) Principles of service and assistance:

c. fast, safe and empathetic;
d. existence of confidentiality guarantee;
e. easily accessible; and
f. free of charge.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with standard operating procedures.

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 16

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in article 15 paragraph (2), shall be provided guidance by the regional government through regional apparatus organizations related to the tasks of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) Organizational guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may consist of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is aimed at providing prevention, protection and services to women and children from acts of violence.

Article 10

(1) In addition to establishing the PPT as referred to in Article 9, to support the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, the regional government may establish P2TP2A.

(2) The P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements of the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Health Service, Social Service, Ministry of Religious Affairs, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Service, NGOs, Child Observers.

(3) The P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), is a functional work unit having the task of implementing integrated services for women and children victims of violence.

(4) In carrying out the main tasks and functions as referred to in paragraph (3), the P2TP2A may coordinate and become a working partner of the PPT. (5) Further provisions regarding the P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), paragraph (3), and paragraph (4), shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 9

(1) In the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which includes prevention and mitigation activities, an Integrated Service Center (PPT) shall be established.

(2) The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements of the Regional Government and elements from related institutions outside the Regional Government.

(3) Further provisions regarding the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be further regulated by Mayor Regulation.

(4) The PPT as referred to in Paragraph (1), in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence may coordinate with institutions and or organizations in Tual City.

(5) In the Implementation of Protection for women and children victims of violence, it may be established at the sub-district, urban village and village levels.

CHAPTER V

FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION

Article 15

(1) The Government in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence. May involve community participation. (2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1), may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

Article 18

(1) The regional government is obligated to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence. (2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of:

a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 13

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for residents of Tual City both in Tual City and outside Tual City.

Article 16

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in article 15 paragraph (2), shall be provided guidance by the regional government through regional apparatus organizations related to the tasks of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) Organizational guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may consist of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tual City.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and Regional House of Representatives according to the principle of autonomy and Co-Administration Task with the principle of the broadest possible autonomy within the system and principle of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Mayor is the Mayor of Tual.
5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Implementation is all actions carried out by government and non-government institutions which include prevention, protection and recovery for victims of violence against women and children.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, and not yet married including a child still in the womb.
8. Woman is every person who is physically born as a woman.
9. Victim is a woman and or child who experiences suffering and or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Prevention is all efforts carried out by government and non-government institutions aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children.
11. Child protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Women protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Suffering is any act that results in or can result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.
14. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting or causing death.
15. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling helpless, and or severe psychological suffering to women and or children.
16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
17. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim, when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
18. Companion is a person or institution that has the ability to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, legal services and advocacy for strengthening victim recovery.
19. Women and child protection institution is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (Including Medicolegal), psycho-social and legal services.
20. Safe house is temporary housing used to provide protection to women and children victims in accordance with the standard operating procedures or abbreviated as SOP that are determined.
21. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or other community organizations.
22. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, hospital-based, community health centers, P2TP2A, Safe Houses, Child Social Protection Houses (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection Houses (RPTC), Women's Social Protection Houses (RPSW).
23. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence in a comprehensive and quality manner.

Article 14

(1) Forms of protection for women and children victims of violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), psychological protection, repatriation and social reintegration.

(2) Forms of medical protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1). Consist of treatment and recovery of physical wounds aimed at recovering the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(3) Forms of legal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.

(5) Forms of psychological protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of assistance in the framework of recovery of traumatic conditions of victims including the provision of Safe Houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.

(6) Forms of Repatriation protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

(7) Forms of Social Reintegration protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to reunite women and children victims of violence with family, substitute family.

Article 2

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is aimed at providing prevention, protection and services to women and children from acts of violence.

Article 11

(1) The Implementation of Protection for victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner in medical handling, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which may be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.

(2) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(3) Principles of service and assistance:

c. fast, safe and empathetic;
d. existence of confidentiality guarantee;
e. easily accessible; and
f. free of charge.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Article 13

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for residents of Tual City both in Tual City and outside Tual City.

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of its promulgation. In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Tual City.

1.7.text:
Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.

Article 14

(1) Forms of protection for women and children victims of violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), psychological protection, repatriation and social reintegration.

(2) Forms of medical protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1). Consist of treatment and recovery of physical wounds aimed at recovering the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(3) Forms of legal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.

(5) Forms of psychological protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of assistance in the framework of recovery of traumatic conditions of victims including the provision of Safe Houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.

(6) Forms of Repatriation protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

(7) Forms of Social Reintegration protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to reunite women and children victims of violence with family, substitute family.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tual City.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and Regional House of Representatives according to the principle of autonomy and Co-Administration Task with the principle of the broadest possible autonomy within the system and principle of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Mayor is the Mayor of Tual.
5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration.
6. Implementation is all actions carried out by government and non-government institutions which include prevention, protection and recovery for victims of violence against women and children.
7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, and not yet married including a child still in the womb.
8. Woman is every person who is physically born as a woman.
9. Victim is a woman and or child who experiences suffering and or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Prevention is all efforts carried out by government and non-government institutions aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children.
11. Child protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Women protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Suffering is any act that results in or can result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.
14. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting or causing death.
15. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling helpless, and or severe psychological suffering to women and or children.
16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
17. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim, when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
18. Companion is a person or institution that has the ability to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, legal services and advocacy for strengthening victim recovery.
19. Women and child protection institution is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (Including Medicolegal), psycho-social and legal services.
20. Safe house is temporary housing used to provide protection to women and children victims in accordance with the standard operating procedures or abbreviated as SOP that are determined.
21. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or other community organizations.
22. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, hospital-based, community health centers, P2TP2A, Safe Houses, Child Social Protection Houses (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection Houses (RPTC), Women's Social Protection Houses (RPSW).

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 11

(1) The Implementation of Protection for victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner in medical handling, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which may be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.

(2) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(3) Principles of service and assistance:

c. fast, safe and empathetic;
d. existence of confidentiality guarantee;
e. easily accessible; and
f. free of charge.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Article 13

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for residents of Tual City both in Tual City and outside Tual City.

Article 16

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in article 15 paragraph (2), shall be provided guidance by the regional government through regional apparatus organizations related to the tasks of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) Organizational guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may consist of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 15

(1) The Government in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence. May involve community participation. (2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1), may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. Article 15

Article 14

(1) Forms of protection for women and children victims of violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), psychological protection, repatriation and social reintegration.

(2) Forms of medical protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1). Consist of treatment and recovery of physical wounds aimed at recovering the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(6) Forms of Repatriation protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

(7) Forms of Social Reintegration protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to reunite women and children victims of violence with family, substitute family.

Article 19

(1) The funding source for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence conducted by the regional apparatus of Tual City is from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Tual City.

Article 13

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for residents of Tual City both in Tual City and outside Tual City.

11. Child protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Women protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Suffering is any act that results in or can result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.
14. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or defects on a person's body, miscarriage, fainting or causing death.
15. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling helpless, and or severe psychological suffering to women and or children.
16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
17. Service is action taken as soon as possible to the victim, when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
18. Companion is a person or institution that has the ability to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, legal services and advocacy for strengthening victim recovery.
19. Women and child protection institution is an institution providing services to victims of violence, hospital-based, managed jointly in the form of medical services (Including Medicolegal), psycho-social and legal services.
20. Safe house is temporary housing used to provide protection to women and children victims in accordance with the standard operating procedures or abbreviated as SOP that are determined.
21. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or other community organizations.
22. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence, hospital-based, community health centers, P2TP2A, Safe Houses, Child Social Protection Houses (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection Houses (RPTC), Women's Social Protection Houses (RPSW).
23. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence in a comprehensive and quality manner.

(1) In addition to establishing the PPT as referred to in Article 9, to support the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence, the regional government may establish P2TP2A.

(2) The P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements of the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Court, Health Service, Social Service, Ministry of Religious Affairs, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Service, NGOs, Child Observers.

(3) The P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), is a functional work unit having the task of implementing integrated services for women and children victims of violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 18

(1) The regional government is obligated to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence. (2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of:

a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

Article 19

(1) The funding source for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence conducted by the regional apparatus of Tual City is from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Tual City.

(2) The funding source as referred to in paragraph (1), may also come from other legitimate and non-binding sources.

(3) The funding source for implementation from other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be supervised in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) PPT is required to report the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence periodically to the Mayor of Tual in accordance with applicable regulations.

Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.

Article 2

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is aimed at providing prevention, protection and services to women and children from acts of violence.

Article 9

(1) In the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence which includes prevention and mitigation activities, an Integrated Service Center (PPT) shall be established.

(2) The PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall consist of elements of the Regional Government and elements from related institutions outside the Regional Government.

(3) Further provisions regarding the PPT as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be further regulated by Mayor Regulation.

(4) The PPT as referred to in Paragraph (1), in implementing protection for women and children victims of violence may coordinate with institutions and or organizations in Tual City.

(5) In the Implementation of Protection for women and children victims of violence, it may be established at the sub-district, urban village and village levels.

(7) Forms of Social Reintegration protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to reunite women and children victims of violence with family, substitute family.

Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 11

(1) The Implementation of Protection for victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner in medical handling, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which may be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.

(2) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(3) Principles of service and assistance:

c. fast, safe and empathetic;
d. existence of confidentiality guarantee;
e. easily accessible; and
f. free of charge.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Article 19

(1) The funding source for the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence conducted by the regional apparatus of Tual City is from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Tual City.

(2) The funding source as referred to in paragraph (1), may also come from other legitimate and non-binding sources.

(3) The funding source for implementation from other legitimate sources as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be supervised in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) PPT is required to report the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence periodically to the Mayor of Tual in accordance with applicable regulations.

Article 14

(1) Forms of protection for women and children victims of violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), psychological protection, repatriation and social reintegration.

(2) Forms of medical protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1). Consist of treatment and recovery of physical wounds aimed at recovering the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(3) Forms of legal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 14

(1) Forms of protection for women and children victims of violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), psychological protection, repatriation and social reintegration.

(2) Forms of medical protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1). Consist of treatment and recovery of physical wounds aimed at recovering the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.

(3) Forms of legal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.

(4) Forms of medicolegal protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consist of medical services for the purposes of evidence in the field of law.

(5) Forms of psychological protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), consist of assistance in the framework of recovery of traumatic conditions of victims including the provision of Safe Houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in problem solving.

(6) Forms of Repatriation protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

(7) Forms of Social Reintegration protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are efforts to reunite women and children victims of violence with family, substitute family.

Article 11

(1) The Implementation of Protection for victims shall be carried out in an integrated manner in medical handling, legal protection, medicolegal, psychological and economic aspects, the implementation of which may be conducted through partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.

(2) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), must pay attention to religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.

(3) Principles of service and assistance:

c. fast, safe and empathetic;
d. existence of confidentiality guarantee;
e. easily accessible; and
f. free of charge.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Article 18

(1) The regional government is obligated to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence. (2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted with the principles of:

a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The implementation of protection for victims of violence is conducted based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. Therefore, every person must obtain their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of just and civilized humanity. In principle, the strategic target of the implementation of protection is to maintain the sustainability of protection through integrated, comprehensive services and a safe and comfortable shelter that is conducive for victims of violence. These strategic targets are pursued through interrelated stages, including planning, protection, services and financing, supervision and sanctions.

Therefore, a legal umbrella in the form of a Regional Regulation is needed that is capable of accommodating all issues related to the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence, capable of providing integrated services holistically and comprehensively, and explicitly providing a mandate to institutions to coordinate policies and supervision, and a mandate to institutions to provide services. In addition, regional regulations can also open the involvement of non-governmental institutions and the community to play a broad role.

Based on several considerations above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.

Article 2

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence is aimed at providing prevention, protection and services to women and children from acts of violence.

Article 16

(1) Social community organizations that participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in article 15 paragraph (2), shall be provided guidance by the regional government through regional apparatus organizations related to the tasks of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) Organizational guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), may consist of social guidance, skills guidance and operational technical guidance.

Article 13

(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions.

(2) Protection for women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for residents of Tual City both in Tual City and outside Tual City.

Article 19

(2) The funding source as referred to in paragraph (1), may also come from other legitimate and non-binding sources.

Article 12

(1) Forms of violence against women and children include physical, psychological, sexual, neglect, exploitation and other violence.

(2) Forms of physical violence consist of any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage of a fetus in the womb and or causes death.

(3) Forms of sexual violence consist of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or specific purposes.

(4) Forms of psychological violence consist of acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feeling of helplessness.

(5) Forms of neglect violence consist of intentional or unintentional acts that result in the non-fulfillment of basic needs. (6) Forms of exploitation violence are forms of violence including acts of economic or sexual exploitation of children for the benefit of oneself or others, acts with or without the consent of the victim but not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully, transferring or transplanting organs and or body tissues or exploiting or the ability of a person to gain profit.
